title: fix(plugin-dashboard): route the sub-caption bundle limb to dataset-bound KPI tiles
body:
Fixes #8889

`tWidgetSubCaption` composes two channels for a metric tile's sub-caption. objectui#7293 / PR #8887
landed limb 1 on the dataset-bound path — the authored `widget.options.description`, collapsed to
the active language — and with it the server-overlay path, since `translateDashboard` writes the
resolved translation onto that same key. **Limb 2 could not follow**: a client i18n bundle entry at
`{ns}.dashboards.{dash}.widgets.{id}.subCaption` needs the dashboard NAME, and neither dispatch
site handed `DatasetWidget` anything but `widget` and `dataSource`.

So a dashboard loaded from an **app bundle**, whose sub-caption was written only in the bundle and
not as `options.description`, rendered **nothing** on a dataset-bound tile — a shape
`tWidgetSubCaption`'s own docblock calls legitimate ("A translation with no authored counterpart is
legitimate and matches the server") — and a tile declaring both rendered the untranslated authored
English.

## Route 2, per the dispatch verdict (comment 5609489952)

The resolution moves into a new `useWidgetSubCaption` hook and **both** dashboard surfaces pass the
**resolved answer** down. `DatasetWidget` is never handed the INPUTS.

The criterion is the number of decision points, not the size of the diff. This field's stated
invariant is that "a bundle entry always wins over an inline map and **the two channels can never
disagree**", and an invariant of that shape needs one decision point to be worth anything. Handing
`DatasetWidget` a `dashName` would put a second copy of the composition inside it, and two copies
can drift — the per-block divergence class objectui#8767 / #8221 keep filing.

`DashboardRenderer`'s private `useCallback` is now a call to that hook; the limbs, their order and
the "undefined, never empty string" contract are unchanged, which is why every pin in
`__tests__/DashboardRenderer.metricSubCaption.test.tsx` stayed put.

### Both dispatch sites are changed — objectui#4614's lesson, mechanically pinned

`DashboardRenderer` and `DashboardGridLayout` both route a dataset-bound widget to the same
component, so a fix wired into one leaves the other silently unchanged. Both now pass
`subCaption={tWidgetSubCaption(widget) ?? null}`. **The suite catches the one-site version** — see
ablation leg B below.

### The prop has three states, and two of them are not the same

- **omitted** — nobody upstream resolved it: no dashboard surface, therefore no dashboard name and
  no bundle key. `DatasetWidget` resolves the authored limb for itself, exactly as #7293 left it.
- **a string** — that is the answer.
- **`null`** — a surface DID resolve it, to nothing. Render nothing, and do **not** fall back to the
  authored value: a bundle entry that resolves to empty is the bundle winning, and the inline arms
  of `getComponentSchema()` render nothing in that same case. Falling back is how the dataset tile
  and the inline arms would start to disagree — the very thing this PR exists to prevent.

## Discriminating power: measured in both directions

Every case was run against the fix **and** against an ablation of it (dispatch sites reverted, bytes
proven on disk, restored from `HEAD` and hash-verified). Directions were written before the runs.

| case | shape | ablated | with fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1/S2 | bundle-only sub-caption, no authored value, per surface | **RED** | green |
| S3/S4 | bundle AND authored (plain string, and inline locale map), per surface | **RED** | green |
| C1 | authored only, NO bundle entry (string + locale map), per surface | green | green |
| C2 | neither channel — no caption node at all, per surface | green | green |
| C3 | no surface at all: `DatasetWidget` with the prop omitted | green | green |

⚠️ **S3/S4 is a SUBJECT, not a control, and the dispatch's wording asked for it as a control.**
"A tile that also declares `options.description` must render bundle-over-authored" is exactly what
is broken on the dataset path today, so it moves with the subject by construction — it cannot be
green before. The assertions that genuinely discriminate are **C1** (this PR delivers limb 2 without
replacing limb 1 — an implementation that swapped one for the other reds here) and the untouched
`DashboardRenderer.metricSubCaption.test.tsx`, whose `(f)` direction pins bundle-over-authored on the
INLINE arm and is green on both sides of the ablation.

### Ablation, run twice

Leg A — **both** dispatch sites reverted: `Tests 6 failed | 29 passed (35)`. The 6 are exactly
S1–S4 across the two surfaces. Every C case, all of `DatasetWidget.subCaption.test.tsx` (#7293's
pins) and all of `DashboardRenderer.metricSubCaption.test.tsx` stayed green.

Leg B — **only** `DashboardGridLayout` reverted, i.e. the one-site fix: `Tests 3 failed | 32 passed
(35)`, and the 3 are the grid surface's S cases alone. A one-site fix does not pass.

Both legs proved the mutation reached disk before reading anything (marker count 1 to 0 per file,
asserted), and both restored via `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` with `git diff HEAD` empty and
each blob hash compared against its `HEAD` blob. A first attempt at leg A is recorded as **void**,
not as a red: it passed a reporter flag vitest 4 does not have, so its `exit 1` was a startup error
that never reached a test body.

## The four readings the dispatch told me not to take on faith

**1. Can `DashboardGridLayout` reach the composed value? YES.** It receives
`schema: DashboardComponentSchema`, which extends `BaseSchema` and therefore declares
`name?: string` — no cast needed, unlike the sibling's historical `schema as any`. And
`useObjectLabel` / `useObjectTranslation` are both provider-safe (objectui#5564), which this surface
needs because it is registered as the `dashboard-grid` SDUI component and renders standalone. So the
hook mounts there with no new requirement on any host.

**2. Is `DatasetWidget` exported from the package barrel? NO — measured, not assumed.**
`packages/plugin-dashboard/package.json` declares exactly one export path, `"."`, resolving to
`dist/index.d.ts`. Built `dist` before and after and compared every `.d.ts` by sha256:

- `dist/index.d.ts` — **byte-identical**, `e76ecfb5655d0727...` on both sides, and it mentions
  `DatasetWidget` zero times. The reachable published type surface does not move at all.
- `dist/DatasetWidget.d.ts` — hash changed (gains `subCaption?: string | null`).
- `dist/widgetSubCaption.d.ts` — new file (`useWidgetSubCaption`, `SubCaptionWidget`).

Those last two are shipped bytes (`files: ["dist"]`) but are **not resolvable** through the exports
map, so no consumer can import them. Clause-② is nonetheless declared **yes** — see below.

**3. The card's line numbers were re-derived, not copied.** `DatasetWidget.tsx` had moved under
PR #8887. Everything in this PR and in the new test file cites **anchors**, not line numbers.

**4. The server-overlay channel is untouched.** `translateDashboard` is not in this diff. A served
dashboard still arrives with the translation already written into `options.description` and reaches
the screen through limb 1, which this PR does not change — pinned by C1 and by the existing
"renders the value the server overlaid onto the key" case in `DatasetWidget.subCaption.test.tsx`.

## i18n keys: zero added

Nothing needed one — this card connects an EXISTING key's path. The `i18n-locales` chunk is defined
in `apps/console/vite.config.ts` as `packages/i18n/` only, and this diff changes zero bytes under
`packages/i18n/`, so that chunk's payload is provably unmoved. `check:eager-closure` itself is
**NOT MEASURED** locally: it exits 2, PREREQUISITE NOT MET, because it needs a console build to
weigh anything. Declared to CI.

## Verification

All under the shared heavy-verify lock; verdicts quoted from the runner's own `VERDICT command-exit`
line, never a bare `$?`.

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard type-check` — `VERDICT command-exit 0`
  (it is spelled `type-check` in this repo, and the log echoes both `tsc` invocations).
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-dashboard/` — `VERDICT command-exit 0`,
  **102 files, 916 tests, all passing** (run from the repo root, per AGENTS.md's one correct spelling).
- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-dashboard^...' build` (dependency closure) — `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm exec eslint .` in `packages/plugin-dashboard` — exit 0, **132 files, 0 errors**, 450
  pre-existing warnings; the two new files contribute **zero** of them.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — exit 0, 1 changeset declared for 3 published source files.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over all six paths — exit 0,
  **NOT GOVERNED**, 6 paths checked against 5 governed surfaces, none matched.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes` — exit 0. Plus a direct scan of the six changed paths for the
  non-NUL control range: no hits.
- `pnpm check:unreferenced-sources` — exit 0; the new module is reached from the declared entry point.
- `pnpm check:i18n-keys` — exit 0. `pnpm check:i18n-dead-keys` — exit 0 (report).
- `pnpm check:eager-closure` — **exit 2, NOT MEASURED** (needs a console build), reasoned about above.

## 验收备注

**Position axis: (B) — computed/prose only. No stored, key-or-equality carrier is affected.**
`scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs`'s `UNGATED_EXAMPLES` — the confirmed carrier whose keys embed
line numbers — has **zero** rows into any file in this diff (none of the three edited files carries
an `@example` block at all). The census (`census:cross-file-line-citations`, report-only, exit 0) was
run on `f52a9d7ad` in a throwaway detached worktree and again here, and diffed. It reports 400-plus
drifted rows repo-wide on both sides. This diff's line shifts changed the offsets it prints for a
handful of prose citations into `DatasetWidget.tsx` / `DashboardGridLayout.tsx`, and flipped three
from "non-substantive / unreported" to "drifted". **Deliberately not repaired**: every one of those
anchors is a generic identifier the census matched by coincidence (`dataKey`, `dataSource`,
`element`), several were already pointing at unrelated code on `main` before this branch existed,
and two of the three sit in `packages/types`. Writing fresh numbers derived from a coincidental
token match would state a precision those citations never had. `origin/main` is still `f52a9d7ad`,
so this branch's tree IS the `merge --no-ff` result tree and the census reading above is that
reading.

**Landing order — PR #8905 is open on the same file.** It also modifies
`packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DatasetWidget.tsx` (+41) in the metric-tile region, for objectui#8894
part (b). Both are draft; whichever lands second may need a textual merge in that block. Flagged, not
acted on.

**Noted, not filed.** The `DashboardGridLayout` dispatch site's own comment says the sibling wraps
its widget as `effectiveWidget` "only to merge in the dashboard FILTER BAR's scoped filter, which
this surface does not have" — that asymmetry is still true and is not touched here. Successor: none
queued; it would ride the next card that gives this surface a filter bar.

## Follow-up: the census this change broke, and the enumeration axis that missed it

`676d6be4` went red on CI shard 2/4 in `packages/sdui-parser`'s renderer-consumed-keys census.

### Why the declared narrowing could not have caught it — the generalizable form

The first round's content axis was enumerated toward **downstream consumers**: who calls the helper,
who imports the package, whose behaviour changes. Every one of those is inside `plugin-dashboard`,
and that package's whole suite was green (102 files, 916 tests).

⭐ **But an instrument does not have to live where the behaviour lives.** This census sits in
`packages/sdui-parser` and watches `packages/plugin-dashboard`'s **source text** — file paths, a
directory walk, a hard-coded file list. Enumerating by "who calls me" cannot reach it by
construction, because nothing calls it and it imports none of my files.

⇒ **The content axis has to be enumerated in BOTH directions: downstream consumers (who runs my
code?) AND upstream watchers (who reads my file's source text, path, shape, or the fact of its
existence?) — and a watcher may live in any package.** Corroboration: objectui#8894's implementer hit
this same instrument from the same file. Creating a new file tripped the same one.

### What actually failed — two legs, not the one CI's digest showed

CI surfaced only the leg-4 assertion. Running the file locally showed **two** failures:

- **leg 3** — `DashboardRenderer still reads options.description for the subCaption channel`. It
  text-matched `(widget.options as …)?.description` inside `DashboardRenderer.tsx`, and this PR moved
  that read into `widgetSubCaption.ts`.
- **leg 4** — the repo tripwire for new files reading `widget.options`.

### The verdict on each, read from the instrument's own contract

**leg 4 — `widgetSubCaption.ts` belongs in the list. Not an over-capture.** The list is defined by the
tripwire's own comment as every non-test source file under `packages` / `apps` matching the receiver
spelling, and "a new entry means a new consumer of the bag: re-run the census before extending either
this list or the accepted-key set." Two entries on it are prose-only matches, documented as such
(`useObjectLabel.ts`, the census module itself). **Mine is not one of them**: it carries the actual
read, `(widget.options as …)?.description`, under exactly the spelling the tripwire watches. It is a
first-class consumer, so it is added — with the census re-run, not with the number made to agree.
The **accepted key set is unchanged**: the file reads `description` and nothing else, that key was
already accepted, and leg 2's `DatasetWidget` read set still measures the same six.

**leg 3 — the read did not disappear, it moved; the anchor follows it.** The leg's own comment says
"if this read disappears, `description` needs re-triage, not silent retention". It did not disappear:
the same expression now lives in `widgetSubCaption.ts` and is called by both surfaces. ⚠️ **Re-pointing
the path alone would have been WEAKER than what the leg held** — it would stay green with the read
stranded in a module nothing calls — so the reachability half is now asserted explicitly, and for
**both** surfaces. That is objectui#4614's property, pinned by the census for the first time.

Ablated to prove the new half bites: deleting the grid surface's `useWidgetSubCaption(...)` call reds
**exactly** that one assertion (`Tests 1 failed | 11 passed (12)`), restored from `HEAD` with
`git diff HEAD` empty and the blob hash matched.

The census module's own header named `DashboardRenderer.tsx` as that read site, so this PR made that
paragraph false and corrects it in the same stroke — it is the single-sourced statement leg 3 exists
to defend. Nothing was skipped, disabled, quarantined, or relaxed, and no census criterion was edited.

### Same-class sweep: what else watches these files

Enumerated mechanically over all **2,855** tracked test files, in the watcher direction:

- **7** name one of the four touched source files by path.
- **84** walk `packages` / `apps` / repo root or shell out to `git ls-files` — i.e. can see a new file
  appear regardless of who imports it.

All 91 were run together: **`Test Files 91 passed (91)`, `Tests 2598 passed (2598)`**. The census was
the only one affected, for a reason that is legible rather than lucky: the others key on things this
diff does not move — retired-key scans (the new file introduces no key), `forwardRef` and
`vi.mock` shape guards (it has neither), package-manifest / dist / alias closure checks (no manifest
or build config changed), doc and skills scans (no docs touched), and
`scripts/__tests__/unconsumed-widget-option-claim-6186.test.ts`, whose repo-wide `thresholds` scan is
unaffected because the new file reads only `description`.

CI's own **shard 2/4 — the one that was red — now runs green locally**: `VERDICT command-exit 0`,
`Test Files 715 passed | 1 skipped (716)`, `Tests 9431 passed | 1 skipped (9432)`.

Also re-run after the repair: `packages/sdui-parser/` suite (`13 files / 182 tests`, exit 0);
`check-changeset-presence` exit 0 (7 published source files across 2 released packages, 1 changeset —
the changeset now records that the `sdui-parser` half releases nothing: census test plus one prose
paragraph, no runtime behaviour); `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the two new paths — NOT
GOVERNED; control-byte scan of both — clean.
